close_reason: Added a Deserialize dispatch contract section (None|Some("PartialDate")→PartialDate, Some("Timestamp")→Timestamp, Some(other)→Unknown) and an Error context section (custom strings without anchor in parent Anniversary; callers wrap+context) to the AnniversaryDate doc-comment. Note: the empty-string-as-sentinel ambiguity from contract gap (1) was already removed by bd:JMAP-sgrr.26's refactor; the doc-comment now reflects the cleaned-up behavior. The Unknown round-trip asymmetry overlap with bd:JMAP-sgrr.9 remains open as a separate bead. Pre-commit gate clean. Commit pending.
description:
lib.rs:967-997 implements Serialize and Deserialize for AnniversaryDate
manually because '#[serde(tag = "@type", other)] with tuple variants is not
supported by the derive macro' (lib.rs:954-955).

The Deserialize path at line 977 has two contract gaps the caller may not
expect:

1. Tag normalization (lib.rs:990). The match arms treat empty string and
   the literal 'PartialDate' identically. RFC 9553 §1.3.4 says the default
   type may be omitted, but it does NOT say 'PartialDate' literal is
   interchangeable with omission. A peer that defensively always sends
   '@type': 'PartialDate' deserializes correctly here — but a future change
   to make the dispatch stricter would silently change parsing. The doc
   comment on AnniversaryDate (lib.rs:943-955) does not document the
   tag-normalization semantics.

2. Error message quality (lib.rs:984, 991). Both branches call
   serde_json::from_value(v).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom). The error
   message a caller sees on a malformed Timestamp input would say
   something like 'missing field utc' — but with no anchor to where in the
   parent Anniversary the date field was. Callers debugging a deeply nested
   ContactCard will not get a useful pointer.

3. The Unknown branch (line 994) accepts a serde_json::Value that may not
   round-trip. This overlaps with JMAP-sgrr.9 but the manual-impl context is
   distinct: JMAP-sgrr.9 is about the Rust constructor reachability;
   the contract gap here is that the doc-comment on AnniversaryDate at line
   943-955 does not warn the caller about which @type values fall through
   to Unknown vs. fail to parse.

Resolution: document the dispatch contract on the AnniversaryDate enum: 'When
deserializing, @type values "" (omitted) and "PartialDate" route to the
PartialDate variant; "Timestamp" routes to Timestamp; all other strings route
to Unknown(Value). Errors in parsing PartialDate or Timestamp surface as
custom-bound serde errors that do not include the path within a parent
Anniversary.' Two sentences in the doc-comment close the gap.
title: AnniversaryDate manual Serialize impl drops error context — Timestamp serialization of an invalid utc field silently succeeds
